evidence.description: Full fresh read of the entire behavioral spec performed this session (four sequential Read passes covering the complete file), REQ-101 through REQ-114 traced end-to-end against their own Acceptance Criteria, Edge Cases, and cross-references. Re-derived REQ-114's THREE-condition kill-switch boundary arithmetic independently (sampleSize>=10/<10 partition is exhaustive and non-overlapping across both the cold-start and colony-wide switches; the ratio branch's strict `>0.20`/`<0.80` boundaries at REQ-105/REQ-114 are symmetric by design (0.80+0.20=1.00) and, unlike the now-fixed absolute-loss branch, are not contradicted by any worked example anywhere in either document -- no fixture anywhere asserts an outcome at exactly ratio=0.20 or rate=0.80 that would conflict with the stated strict operators). Checked REQ-101/102 (self-loan exclusion ordering, gojo-gift lender-gating), REQ-103 (bookkeeping-only constraint unchanged), REQ-104-108 (fixed loan terms, txHash same-loan and cross-loan replay rejection, exact zero-padded to/from address-equality attribution), REQ-109 (append-only default detection, debt-proportional balance adjustment, defaulted_ms field), REQ-110-113 (gig-coexistence zero-coupling, money-safety invariant, single-coordinator-host scope, dependency-freshness gate) -- no internal contradiction, no unreachable worked example, and no unresolved FIND found in any of these beyond the two already-tracked and now-resolved FIND-701/FIND-702.

Re-read REQ-114's entire section fresh, specifically hunting for a second boundary/off-by-one bug of the same class as FIND-701 per the task's own instruction to scrutinize this area further. Found none: the ratio-based branch's own strict inequality is internally consistent with every worked example in the document (no fixture computes an exact-boundary case for the ratio, unlike the absolute-loss branch's now-fixed prior defect, which had two directly conflicting worked examples in the SAME document). The sampleSize>=10/sampleSize<10 partition used identically by both REQ-105's and REQ-114's kill-switches is exhaustive with no gap or overlap.

Full fresh read of the entire verification architecture performed this session (three sequential Read passes covering the complete 462-line file), all Proof Obligation rows (PROP-101a through PROP-113a, including PROP-109g and the full PROP-114 family) and the full 11-item Gate section traced against their corresponding REQ text in behavioral-spec.md. Confirmed every REQ has at least one Gate item, every Tier-0 structural check for a 'real code, not a mock/fixture' fact (PROP-105h, PROP-106d, PROP-106i, PROP-109g, PROP-111a/b, PROP-112a, PROP-114c) is present and specifically worded to reject a mocked-caller or hand-authored-fixture proof as sufficient, and the Verification Strategy's Tier 0/1/2/3 breakdown correctly cites every PROP by ID with no orphaned required:true obligation missing from either the Verification Strategy section or the Gate section.
